content: Diphenhydramine is an antihistamine that is specifically used to alleviate itching caused by insect bites, sunburns, bee stings, poison ivy, poison oak, and minor skin irritations. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes, so it is important to consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Diphenhydramine topical is available in various forms, including cream, lotion, gel, and spray, and it is intended for application directly to the skin. It should be used three to four times daily. Follow the instructions provided on the packaging or your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions or need clarification, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Use the medication exactly as directed, without exceeding or reducing the recommended amount or frequency. Before application, clean the affected area thoroughly, allow it to dry, and then gently rub the medication into the skin until most of it is absorbed. Use only enough to cover the affected area. After applying the medication, wash your hands thoroughly. Do not use diphenhydramine on chickenpox or measles, and avoid using it on children under the age of 2 unless specifically instructed by a doctor. Before using diphenhydramine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to diphenhydramine or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, including vitamins and supplements. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while using diphenhydramine, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed application. Diphenhydramine may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: skin rash, sunburn, or increased sensitivity to sunlight or sunlamps. Store diphenhydramine in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. The spray form of this medication is flammable, so keep it away from open flames and extreme heat. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Diphenhydramine is intended for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not ingest it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin products to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If your skin condition worsens or does not improve, inform your doctor. Keep all scheduled appointments with your healthcare provider. If you have any questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Diphenhydramine is available under various brand names, including: Benadryl® Itch Relief Stick Extra Strength Benadryl® Itch Stopping Cream Extra Strength Benadryl® Itch Stopping Cream Original Strength Benadryl® Itch Stopping Extra Strength Spray Benadryl® Itch Stopping Gel Extra Strength Benadryl® Itch Stopping Gel Original Strength Benadryl® Itch Stopping Original Strength Spray Dermamycin® Combination products containing diphenhydramine include: Dermamycin® Spray (Diphenhydramine Hydrochloride and Menthol) Dermarest® Maximum Strength (Diphenhydramine Hydrochloride and Resorcinol) Dermarest® Plus (Diphenhydramine Hydrochloride and Menthol) Di-Delamine® (Diphenhydramine Hydrochloride and Tripelennamine)
